# Configure TLS for listeners

Boundary assumes TLS is enabled on `api` and `ops` listeners. This page describes how to provide a certificate and key to a TCP or Unix listener, how to require client certificates, and how to restrict TLS versions.

## Requirements

- A certificate file and a private key file in PEM format. To use a certificate authority (CA) certificate, concatenate the primary certificate and the CA certificate into a single file. The primary certificate must appear first.
- Read access to both files for the user that runs Boundary.

TLS parameters apply to `api` and `ops` listeners. The `cluster` and `proxy` connections use their own ephemeral TLS stacks. Refer to [TLS in Boundary](/boundary/docs/secure/encryption/connections-tls) for more information.

## Enable TLS on a listener

Boundary requires a certificate on any `api` or `ops` listener that does not set `tls_disable = true`. If you omit `tls_cert_file`, Boundary fails to start the listener.

1. Open the Boundary configuration file.
1. In the `listener` stanza, set `tls_cert_file` and `tls_key_file` to the paths of the certificate and key.

   <Tabs>

   <Tab heading="TCP listener" group="tcp">

   ```hcl
   listener "tcp" {
     purpose       = "api"
     tls_cert_file = "/etc/certs/Boundary.crt"
     tls_key_file  = "/etc/certs/Boundary.key"
   }
   ```

   </Tab>

   <Tab heading="Unix listener" group="unix">

   ```hcl
   listener "unix" {
     purpose       = "api"
     address       = "/var/run/boundary-api.sock"
     tls_cert_file = "/etc/certs/Boundary.crt"
     tls_key_file  = "/etc/certs/Boundary.key"
   }
   ```

   </Tab>

   </Tabs>

1. Start or restart Boundary.

If the key file is encrypted, Boundary prompts for the passphrase when it starts.

## Require client certificates

To require clients to present a certificate, set `tls_require_and_verify_client_cert` to `true`. Optionally, set `tls_client_ca_file` to the path of a PEM-encoded CA file that Boundary uses to verify the client certificate. If you omit `tls_client_ca_file`, Boundary verifies client certificates against the system CAs.

```hcl
listener "tcp" {
  purpose                            = "api"
  tls_cert_file                      = "/etc/certs/Boundary.crt"
  tls_key_file                       = "/etc/certs/Boundary.key"
  tls_require_and_verify_client_cert = true
  tls_client_ca_file                 = "/etc/certs/clients-ca.crt"
}
```

## Restrict TLS versions

By default, Boundary accepts TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3. To restrict the accepted range, set `tls_min_version`, `tls_max_version`, or both.

```hcl
listener "tcp" {
  purpose         = "api"
  tls_cert_file   = "/etc/certs/Boundary.crt"
  tls_key_file    = "/etc/certs/Boundary.key"
  tls_min_version = "tls13"
}
```

Accepted values are `tls12` and `tls13`. The value of `tls_max_version` must be greater than or equal to `tls_min_version`. TLS 1.1 and lower are not supported.

## Reload certificates

When Boundary receives a `SIGHUP` signal, it reloads the certificate and key from the paths set at startup. Changing the paths in the configuration file while Boundary is running has no effect on a reload. The passphrase of an encrypted key file must remain the same between reload cycles.
